00A2A5:Oblivion.esm.Name: A Stranger
00A2A5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Corvus Umbranox appears as the Stranger during the final Thieves Guild scene, before reclaiming his identity as the Gray Fox.
00A2A5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies the final-scene Stranger as the Gray Fox himself. His reputation as the greatest of thieves and his documented spellcasting support an elite rating, but not the Gray Cowl’s supernatural curse as personal combat power.

0389B8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Abhuki
0389B8:Oblivion.esm.Description: Khajiit innkeeper, merchant, and advanced Alteration trainer at the Faregyl Inn.
0389B8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her innkeeping and merchant work establish competent professional expertise; her advanced-trainer role supports competence in Alteration, but the evidence does not establish mastery.

0A3166:Oblivion.esm.Name: Achille
0A3166:Oblivion.esm.Description: Achille is a Blade stationed at Cloud Ruler Temple, with no individual accomplishment described in the available article.
0A3166:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His identification as a Blade supports competent professional standing in the Blade discipline; reading a tactics book adds context but does not establish exceptional expertise.
0A3166:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article documents no specific combat feats or further training.

02FB2B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adamus Phillida
02FB2B:Oblivion.esm.Description: A veteran Imperial Legion commander who spent forty years in service and devoted much of his career to investigating and disrupting the Dark Brotherhood.
02FB2B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His decades of service and sustained work against dangerous assassins support a seasoned-combatant rating. The article does not establish elite personal combat mastery or feats warranting a higher tier.

1778DC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adamus Phillida's Bodyguard
1778DC:Oblivion.esm.Description: An unnamed Imperial City Watch bodyguard assigned to Adamus Phillida, sworn to protect him if threatened.
1778DC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His City Watch bodyguard role supports the competent professional-soldier baseline. The article establishes his duty to defend Phillida but no exceptional combat feats.
1778DC:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article does not describe his individual combat training or feats.

01FB56:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adanrel
01FB56:Oblivion.esm.Description: Adanrel is a Waterfront District laborer with limited demonstrated expertise; her available stealth magic and basic weapons suggest basic capability.
01FB56:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article describes her as having few skills and quotes her saying she and other Waterfront workers have no skills. She has no established professional feats; her combat equipment supports only basic capability.

01681B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adeo
01681B:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Dark Seducer captain who leads the surviving defenders and fights alongside the player to reclaim Pinnacle Rock.
01681B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her leadership of the remaining forces and demonstrated participation in combat support seasoned professional capability. Her standard Dark Seducer spells add magical competence, but the evidence does not establish mastery or exceptional individual feats.

0AED40:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adoring Fan
0AED40:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Wood Elf commoner who follows the Arena’s Grand Champion and tends to flee when danger arises.
0AED40:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His commoner identity and behavior establish no specialized professional expertise; he usually avoids combat. Tier 2 reflects the ordinary-adult baseline, not a claim of negligible ability.

02F865:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adosi Serethi
02F865:Oblivion.esm.Description: Aleswell ostler whose documented role provides limited evidence of ordinary professional capability; no exceptional expertise is established.
02F865:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her biography identifies her as an ostler, supporting competent occupational ability. The quest and dialogue show no further professional accomplishments, so a higher tier is unsupported.
02F865:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Her ostler duties and skill are not demonstrated in the article.

016057:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adrian Decanius
016057:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial commoner with no documented specialized profession or notable accomplishments.
016057:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The UESP article identifies Adrian as a commoner. His mace, dagger, and chainmail establish basic equipment, not demonstrated combat expertise; no other specialized discipline is evidenced.
016057:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: No specialized training or professional expertise is documented.

02950A:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adrienne Berene
02950A:Oblivion.esm.Description: Adrienne Berene is a scholarly Breton mage whose destructive magic makes her a dangerous opponent, though her documented abilities do not establish exceptional mastery.
02950A:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her UESP article describes her as a mage with a particularly powerful Destruction repertoire. That supports a seasoned threat, but no distinctive combat feats or demonstrated mastery justify a higher tier.

068828:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adult Rumare Slaughterfish
068828:Oblivion.esm.Description: A mundane aquatic slaughterfish variant found around Lake Rumare; it is an animal without magical or weapon-wielding abilities.
068828:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Its verified form supports an ordinary natural-threat rating; the source establishes no exceptional feats, training, or supernatural abilities.
068828:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The source confirms the Rumare variant but gives no specific feats for this adult individual.

018FD8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adventurer
018FD8:Oblivion.esm.Description: An Orc treasure-seeker sent by Gortwog, encountered in Cyrodiil’s ruins and caves; this record is not identified as a unique hero.
018FD8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Adventurers actively fight creatures during their expeditions, supporting a competent-combatant baseline. The article establishes no individual feats or exceptional mastery.
018FD8:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article describes several class variants but does not identify this record’s class; no exceptional individual feats are established.

185FE0:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aelwin Merowald
185FE0:Oblivion.esm.Description: Aelwin Merowald is an older Breton fisherman whose injury has forced him to stop working and seek help collecting slaughterfish scales.
185FE0:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His years as a working fisherman and his contract to supply scales support competent professional expertise in fishing. The article establishes no exceptional combat or other specialist accomplishments.

0514C4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aengvir
0514C4:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Wood Elf commoner in Harlun’s Watch who lives an ordinary routine and offers limited information during a local investigation.
0514C4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The supplied UESP biography establishes a commoner’s ordinary life but no specialized training or notable professional accomplishments. Tier 2 reflects an ordinary adult with no established specialized expertise.

035726:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aenvir
035726:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Wood Elf hunter and former shop employee who participates in recurring nighttime burglaries with two companions.
035726:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His hunter identity and repeated shop robberies support competent professional capability, including practical stealth and theft. No exceptional accomplishments establish higher expertise.

098254:Oblivion.esm.Name: Afflicted Brethren
098254:Oblivion.esm.Description: A vampire and former worshipper of Azura, one of five afflicted brethren who slew the powerful vampire Dratik before contracting vampirism.
098254:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor is confirmed as a vampire, and the brethren’s shared history of slaying a powerful vampire supports competent combat capability without establishing exceptional individual mastery.

01FC54:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agarmir
01FC54:Oblivion.esm.Description: Agarmir is a professional thief and illicit supplier who conceals his dealings and prepares an ambush when exposed.
01FC54:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His sustained under-the-table supply business, deceptive cover story, coercive bargaining, and planned graveyard trap show practical criminal expertise. The evidence supports a competent professional, not exceptional mastery.

02D028:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agata
02D028:Oblivion.esm.Description: Agata is a Mages Guild Evoker who supports the Leyawiin chapter and helps with its recommendation quest.
02D028:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her established role as a Guild mage supports competent magical ability, but the article gives no combat feats or combat-specific mastery to justify a higher tier.

0C55E5:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agnar the Unwavering
0C55E5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Agnar is a Nord warrior and former Chieftain of Thirsk, found dead after pursuing the Uderfrykte Matron near Dive Rock.
0C55E5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His identity as a warrior supports competent professional capability. The dangerous hunt shows resolve, but the chieftain title and the hunt itself do not establish exceptional combat mastery.
0C55E5:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: No specific combat feats or successful outcome establish a higher level of expertise.

028F9B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agnete the Pickled
028F9B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Agnete is a Skingrad smith and armorer whose repair work is praised by local townspeople.
028F9B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her smithing and armor-repair work is established as reliably fine, supporting a seasoned professional tier. Her shop and unique merchandise support trade expertise, but do not by themselves establish master-level craftsmanship.

037FF8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agronak gro-Malog
037FF8:Oblivion.esm.Description: Agronak gro-Malog, the Gray Prince, is a vampiric-blooded Orc and long-standing Arena Grand Champion whose unusual abilities make him an exceptionally formidable fighter.
037FF8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His nearly decade-long reign and reputation as unbeatable, alongside explicitly heightened abilities from vampiric blood, support elite combat prowess. The evidence does not establish feats warranting legendary mastery.

0293D5:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ah-Malz
0293D5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Ah-Malz is an Argonian blademaster and experienced goblin hunter who regularly spars with a fellow Fighters Guild member.
0293D5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His blademaster identity, expert goblin hunting, and regular sparring support a seasoned-combatant rating, but the article establishes no exceptional feats warranting an elite tier.

034E87:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ahdarji
034E87:Oblivion.esm.Description: Ahdarji is a retired Thieves Guild thief and advanced Light Armor trainer who uses a stolen ring to gather and sell information.
034E87:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her established thief and information-gathering experience, together with advanced Light Armor training, supports seasoned professional capability. The evidence does not establish exceptional mastery.
034E87:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Her former theft accomplishments are described only broadly; exceptional mastery is not established.

0155A0:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ahjazda
0155A0:Oblivion.esm.Description: Ahjazda is a Khajiit enchantress and merchant whose expertise is associated with magic goods, though her demonstrated role is primarily commercial.
0155A0:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her enchantress identity and specialist shop support competent professional standing in her field. She also teaches a confusion spell, but the evidence does not establish exceptional enchanting or magical mastery.
0155A0:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Her actual enchanting work and depth of magical training are not described.

0356CD:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ajum-Kajin
0356CD:Oblivion.esm.Description: Argonian Blackwood Company mage and expansion leader, encountered at Glademist Cave during the Information Gathering quest.
0356CD:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His mage identity and role in an organized company support competent professional capability. He uses mage spells in combat, but no exceptional magical feats are established; his rank alone does not imply mastery.
0356CD:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: His specific magical training and accomplishments are not described.

01C48D:Oblivion.esm.Name: Akaviri Commander Mishaxhi
01C48D:Oblivion.esm.Description: A ghostly Tsaesci commander and renowned Akaviri tactician guarding the Draconian Madstone at Fort Pale Pass.
01C48D:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Identified as one of the Akaviri invasion’s greatest tacticians; he remains armed and guards the fort. This supports highly accomplished military and martial expertise, not legendary individual combat.
01C48D:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: His strategic reputation is explicit, but specific personal combat feats are limited; the tier reflects command and martial expertise, not mastery of every warrior skill.

03C15F:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alawen
03C15F:Oblivion.esm.Description: Alawen is a Wood Elf master marksman who hunts with a bow and trains others in Marksman.
03C15F:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her established mastery as a Marksman trainer supports the project's Master combat trainer baseline. The claim that she is Cyrodiil's best shot is only reported as a rumor and is not needed for this tier.

0222B8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alberic Litte
0222B8:Oblivion.esm.Description: Alberic Litte is a Mages Guild associate and advanced Conjuration trainer who also sells spells and offers practical magical guidance.
0222B8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His advanced Conjuration training role supports seasoned professional expertise in that discipline. His broader mage role and spell-selling are established, but no exceptional personal accomplishments justify a higher tier.

0034DE:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aldos Othran
0034DE:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Dunmer farmer whose established life centers on ordinary labor; his brief, drunken confrontation with a guard shows no specialized expertise.
0034DE:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His wife’s death in a bandit attack left him barely escaping alive. He carries an iron dagger, but no farming mastery or other professional skill is established; his scripted defeat does not prove broader combat ability.
0034DE:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article establishes little about his farming skill, and his scripted death limits what the guard encounter demonstrates.

00A110:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aleron Loche
00A110:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Breton commoner lured into Kurdan’s hunt; he explicitly says he cannot fight and has never held a weapon.
00A110:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His own account establishes very limited combat capability. No specialized professional expertise is evidenced; his gambling and debt do not establish a relevant discipline.

01D346:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alessia Ottus
01D346:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial commoner and author of guidebooks to Cyrodiil’s cities; her writing shows professional authorship but limited analytical depth.
01D346:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her numerous published city guides establish a competent writing and observational discipline. The evidence does not establish exceptional scholarship or specialized combat capability.

035EC4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alga
035EC4:Oblivion.esm.Description: Nord bard and Speechcraft trainer in Bruma, known locally for keeping old songs and stories alive and for her storytelling.
035EC4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her storytelling has a strong local reputation, establishing professional competence in her bardic and social discipline. The article describes her Speechcraft training as basic and gives no evidence of rare mastery or extraordinary accomplishments.

01D344:Oblivion.esm.Name: Algot the Northerner
01D344:Oblivion.esm.Description: Nord bard and Imperial City civilian who does odd jobs and some adventuring; no notable combat training or feats are established.
01D344:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article mentions only a little adventuring, with no evidence of professional training or exceptional ability. The project's ordinary adult civilian baseline applies.

18D2B4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alix Lencolia
18D2B4:Oblivion.esm.Description: Young Breton crusader and master Blade trainer, renowned for his sword skill and associated with the Blade Training quest.
18D2B4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: UESP identifies Alix as the master trainer in Blade and records other trainers calling him famous for his skill with a blade. Established mastery in a combat discipline supports Tier 6.

08595D:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alonzo
08595D:Oblivion.esm.Description: Alonzo is a Redguard bandit boss who leads raids on travelers with members of the Black Bow Bandits.
08595D:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His active role in bandit raids supports competent combat capability, but the article provides no evidence of veteran training or exceptional personal feats.
08595D:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The source establishes his bandit role but does not describe his individual combat skill.

031867:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aloys Bincal
031867:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial farmer and Cropsford settler whose supplied biography establishes no specialized combat or other exceptional expertise.
031867:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His identity and farming occupation are established, but the article provides no specific evidence of advanced farming, combat, or other professional mastery. Basic capability is the best-supported rating.

01207B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Althel's Ghost
01207B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Althel is a cursed Wood Elf scout and defensive archer whose arrows are needed to take part in Vitharn’s battle.
01207B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her patrol spotted the invading force and she rode back to warn Vitharn. She is identified as a scout and archer, but her repeated defeat occurs without arrows; the evidence supports competent professional ability, not exceptional mastery.
01207B:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Her combat skill is difficult to assess because she is unarmed during the recurring encounter.

030196:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alval Uvani
030196:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Dark Elf battlemage and master of Destruction magic, Alval is a dangerous opponent with additional Mysticism and Restoration spells.
030196:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor-specific article identifies him as a master of Destruction and describes him as a formidable opponent. That established magical mastery supports Tier 6; his quest role alone does not raise the tier.

02D027:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alves Uvenim
02D027:Oblivion.esm.Description: Dark Elf alchemist and Mages Guild journeyman; a practiced researcher who advises Rosentia, with no established combat feats or combat specialization.
02D027:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her documented expertise is alchemy and research, not combat. The ordinary-adult baseline is appropriate absent evidence of combat training or demonstrated fighting ability.

08209B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alyssa
08209B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Alyssa was a Breton conjurer, but this Dire Warren encounter represents her corpse after a fatal fall, not her living form.
08209B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The source confirms Alyssa’s identity and conjurer background, but the represented actor is deceased; no combat tier is supported for this corpse.
08209B:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Her living combat ability is not established, and should not be assigned to the corpse without supporting evidence.

0097A5:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amantius Allectus
0097A5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial writer and amateur researcher who authors scholarly works and conducts unusual plant experiments; no specialized combat expertise is established.
0097A5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His authorship and ongoing research support competent professional-level scholarly ability. His role as a Thieves Guild quest target does not establish exceptional stealth or combat skill.

028E75:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ambroise Canne
028E75:Oblivion.esm.Description: A renowned Block specialist whose advanced instruction and local reputation establish him as a highly accomplished defensive combatant.
028E75:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The UESP article identifies Ambroise as an advanced Block trainer and reports that townspeople regard his shield skill as superior to the Fighters Guild trainer’s. This supports an elite specialist rating, but not master-level combat mastery.

01207A:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amiable Fanriene
01207A:Oblivion.esm.Description: Amiable Fanriene is a highly capable Breton conjurer whose formidable spellcasting contrasts with his persistent paranoia.
01207A:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor-specific article describes him as one of the Isles’ most capable mages and details a broad repertoire of powerful spells, supporting a master-level assessment.

026B4C:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amir
026B4C:Oblivion.esm.Description: Redguard assassin and devoted Molag Bal worshipper who helps direct the shrine’s quest.
026B4C:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Identified as an assassin, supporting competent professional standing in that discipline. The article gives no exceptional assassination or stealth accomplishments to justify a higher tier.
026B4C:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: No individual assassination or stealth feats are described.

03CD19:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amkaos
03CD19:Oblivion.esm.Description: Amkaos is a named Dremora torturer and patrol guard in Mankar Camoran’s Paradise, with established armed combat and limited Destruction and Mysticism magic.
03CD19:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His role and equipment support a competent combatant with some magical capability. No exceptional individual accomplishments are documented.
03CD19:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: His personal expertise beyond his documented guard and torturer duties is unclear.

0A369F:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amminus Gregori
0A369F:Oblivion.esm.Description: Cheydinhal City Guard assigned to watch the Oblivion Gate; equipped as a professional guard and armed with a silver longsword.
0A369F:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His guard duties, armor, and weapon support competent professional capability in the Knight discipline. The article establishes no exceptional personal feats or mastery.

000F62:Knights.esp.Name: Amragor
000F62:Knights.esp.Description: Wood Elf healer residing in the Chapel of Dibella, with a set of healer spells and an additional Restoration spell.
000F62:Knights.esp.Reason: His healer role and established healing spell repertoire support competent professional capability in healing and Restoration. The evidence does not establish exceptional mastery or accomplishments.

03563B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amusei
03563B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Argonian freelance thief who later earns a Thieves Guild career and serves as a messenger for the Gray Fox.
03563B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Thievery is his profession, but early failures—including botching the Guild-entry race, getting jailed after stealing a ring, and being caught stealing food—show limited execution. His later Guild advancement and trusted message-running support competent professional capability, not exceptional mastery.

05E1DC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anaxes
05E1DC:Oblivion.esm.Description: Anaxes is a Xivilai lord encountered in Mankar Camoran’s Paradise, where the inhabitants have trapped him in his cave.
05E1DC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The supplied UESP article confirms his Xivilai form. The project baseline assigns verified Xivilai tier 6; unique feats are not required.

0C6573:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancestor Guardian
0C6573:Oblivion.esm.Description: A guardian summoned through the Dunmer Ancestor Guardian ability; its exact creature form is not established by the available evidence.
0C6573:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Manual deleveling review: Loaded ghost model confirms summoned ancestor spirit; ordinary ghost baseline.
0C6573:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Initial balance assignment; editable after in-game testing.
0C6573:Oblivion.esm.DelevelingReview: Loaded ghost model confirms summoned ancestor spirit; ordinary ghost baseline.

05D2BC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancient Ghost
05D2BC:Oblivion.esm.Description: An ancient ghost, a more formidable ghost variant that attacks with frost-focused magic and is described as more dangerous than a standard ghost.
05D2BC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The verified ancient form is explicitly more formidable than the ordinary ghost baseline (tier 3), supporting a modest increase to seasoned threat.

070913:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancient Sanctified Dead
070913:Oblivion.esm.Description: An ancient ghost, a more formidable spectral variant that relies on magical attacks, particularly frost, and is more powerful than a standard ghost.
070913:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor’s identity matches the ancient ghost form. UESP describes ancient ghosts as more formidable than standard ghosts, with more powerful spells, supporting a step above the project’s ordinary ghost baseline.

02F86D:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancotar
02F86D:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Mages Guild wizard and warlock whose magical research made people and creatures across a wide area invisible; he also developed a counterspell.
02F86D:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His demonstrated area-effect spellcraft and ability to devise a counterspell establish substantial magical competence. The evidence supports a seasoned mage, but not exceptional combat mastery.

01D354:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancus Afranius
01D354:Oblivion.esm.Description: A low-ambition bard and Thieves Guild member with no documented exceptional professional accomplishments.
01D354:Oblivion.esm.Reason: UESP identifies Ancus as a bard and Thieves Guild member; his class and bard spells support basic professional capability. No specific feats establish greater expertise, and guild membership alone does not prove mastery of theft.

00A10B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Andragil
00A10B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Wood Elf Bravil resident and master Block trainer who tests trainees by striking them with a warhammer.
00A10B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Andragil is explicitly identified as a master trainer in Block, a combat discipline. Other expert trainers credit her instruction, and her training test demonstrates her ability to withstand a prolonged combat challenge.

0C56E4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Andre Labouche
0C56E4:Oblivion.esm.Description: Andre Labouche is a deceased Breton spellsword whose body and daughter’s note provide a clue to The Horror of Dive Rock.
0C56E4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His spellsword identity and broad magical capability support a trained, competent professional. No evidence establishes exceptional mastery; his climbing failure does not determine his spellsword expertise.

030FDB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Andreas Draconis
030FDB:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial publican who sells food and rents beds at the Drunken Dragon Inn; targeted during the Dark Brotherhood’s Next of Kin quest.
030FDB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His established expertise is ordinary innkeeping and customer service. Interest in brewing does not establish brewing mastery; his quest dialogue shows willingness to fight, but no notable combat expertise.

07E9BB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Androcide
07E9BB:Oblivion.esm.Description: Unverified creature encounter; no actor-specific UESP evidence establishes its form or capabilities.
07E9BB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The supplied record identifies a creature but not its species or lore. Without a verified form, no project baseline can be applied.
07E9BB:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The encounter identity and creature form remain unverified; no suitable actor-specific UESP article was found.
07E9BB:Oblivion.esm.DelevelingReview: Unreferenced skeleton minion record in loaded base plugin; not an active encounter.

026B36:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anedhel
026B36:Oblivion.esm.Description: A competent witch and Clavicus Vile devotee with established Destruction and Mysticism spellcasting.
026B36:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her witch identity and known spells establish professional magical capability, but the evidence gives no accomplishments supporting a higher tier. This rating concerns her magical discipline, not every skill.

0234BB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Angalmo
0234BB:Oblivion.esm.Description: High Elf alchemist and Mages Guild Evoker who offers basic Mysticism training; no combat feats or combat-focused expertise are established.
0234BB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies Angalmo as an adult mortal but establishes no combat training or demonstrated fighting ability. Basic Mysticism training does not establish combat mastery, so the ordinary adult baseline is appropriate.

026ADB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Angalsama
026ADB:Oblivion.esm.Description: Angalsama is a Sheogorath worshipper identified as a High Elf mage; she knows mage spells but has no documented exceptional magical accomplishments.
026ADB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her mage identity and spell knowledge support ordinary professional capability in magic. Her madness and shrine devotion do not establish greater expertise, and lack of combat feats is not a reason to underrate her as a mage.
026ADB:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Her specific magical training and demonstrated spellcasting ability are not described.

01FC51:Oblivion.esm.Name: Angelie
01FC51:Oblivion.esm.Description: Redguard commoner living a reserved life in the Imperial City’s Talos Plaza District.
01FC51:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article establishes ordinary civilian life but no specialized training, professional expertise, or notable accomplishments. Tier 2 reflects the ordinary-adult baseline, not a finding of negligible ability.
01FC51:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article provides little evidence about her abilities beyond her commoner background and routine.

052F61:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anglor's Ghost
052F61:Oblivion.esm.Description: Anglor’s Ghost is a Vitharn conjurer whose demonstrated magical role is supporting Prior Dreth by sacrificing his own Magicka.
052F61:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His conjurer identity and recorded Magicka sacrifice support competent, limited magical expertise. The evidence does not establish mastery or exceptional combat ability.
052F61:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: His broader magical and combat capabilities are not established.

00A299:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anguilon
00A299:Oblivion.esm.Description: Wood Elf pirate and seaman employed aboard The Serpent’s Wake; his documented combat weapon is an iron dagger.
00A299:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His employment as a seaman supports competent professional standing in the pirate’s maritime discipline. No evidence establishes exceptional combat, stealth, or other specialized mastery.
00A299:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article gives little detail about his specific duties or demonstrated seamanship.

0488F3:Oblivion.esm.Name: Antoine Branck
0488F3:Oblivion.esm.Description: A stablehand and horse caretaker at Bay Roan Stables, responsible for tending the horses and preparing purchased horses for customers.
0488F3:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His routine and dialogue establish practical competence in stable work and horse care. The evidence supports professional ability in that role, but not exceptional mastery or combat expertise.

023E36:Oblivion.esm.Name: Antoinetta Marie
023E36:Oblivion.esm.Description: A novice Dark Brotherhood assassin who trains regularly and implies experience with kills, but has no documented exceptional contract or mastery.
023E36:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her assassin identity, references to performing kills, and regular training support an apprentice-level professional assessment. Her newcomer status and lack of specific accomplishments do not support a higher tier.
023E36:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: No particular assassination feat or demonstrated level of skill is documented.

067418:Oblivion.esm.Name: Antus Flonius
067418:Oblivion.esm.Description: An Imperial Fighters Guild apprentice who regularly spars and is equipped as a warrior.
067418:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His Guild training and regular sparring support a competent-fighter baseline, but the article establishes no veteran experience, exceptional mastery, or notable combat feats.

0222A0:Oblivion.esm.Name: Antus Odiil
0222A0:Oblivion.esm.Description: Antus Odiil is a hot-headed farmhand who joins his brother and the player in defending the family farm from goblins.
0222A0:Oblivion.esm.Reason: He can fight with a sword and takes part in the battle, but his brother says Antus has never faced a fight like it; he is also described as the less capable fighter. His enthusiasm and bravery do not establish seasoned expertise.

00A0AE:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anvil Guard
00A0AE:Oblivion.esm.Description: A generic Anvil city guard serving as a soldier of the local count; a trained professional fighter.
00A0AE:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The UESP article identifies county city guards as soldiers serving their local count. The project's professional-soldier baseline supports tier 3.

0034C4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Borba gra-Uzgash
0034C4:Oblivion.esm.Description: Retired adventurer and Cheydinhal shopkeeper with established experience clearing a nearby cave and running a general-goods business.
0034C4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her past adventuring and reported clearing of Quickwater Cave support seasoned practical ability; her active trade supports competent professional mercantile skill. Gang membership alone establishes no further expertise.

034EB0:Oblivion.esm.Name: Borissean
034EB0:Oblivion.esm.Description: Borissean is a renowned Mages Guild spellmaker whose magical mastery spans nearly every type of spell.
034EB0:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Actor-specific accounts describe Borissean and Gaspar Stegine as among Cyrodiil’s most powerful mages, with mastery of nearly every type of spell. This supports the Master tier.

098252:Oblivion.esm.Name: Boroneth
098252:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Wood Elf hunter and Hircine worshipper; her confirmed professional identity supports competent hunter-level capability.
098252:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her hunter identity and bow establish a relevant hunting discipline, but the source records no exceptional feats or demonstrated mastery. Tier 3 reflects a competent professional, not equal strength across all disciplines.

01BC2A:Oblivion.esm.Name: Bosmer Thief
01BC2A:Oblivion.esm.Description: A dead Altmer thief found in the Painted World; he assaulted Rythe Lythandas, stole the Brush of Truepaint, and was killed by the trolls he created.
01BC2A:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The represented encounter form is a corpse, with no meaningful combat capability. His actions as a living thief do not establish combat prowess.

034EB7:Oblivion.esm.Name: Bothiel
034EB7:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Mages Guild wizard and astronomer whose specialist expertise includes understanding and maintaining the Imperial Orrery.
034EB7:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Raminus identifies Bothiel as one of the few who understands how the Orrery works and has kept it running. Her demonstrated magical and technical scholarship supports highly accomplished expertise, without establishing mastery in combat magic.

035EC6:Oblivion.esm.Name: Bradon Lirrian
035EC6:Oblivion.esm.Description: Bradon Lirrian is represented as his corpse, found dead in his Bruma home after Raynil Dralas killed him.
035EC6:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article confirms Bradon is dead and the actor record represents his corpse; the living civilian baseline does not apply to this form.

027F95:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brag gro-Bharg
027F95:Oblivion.esm.Description: Orc barbarian and Fighters Guild Associate assigned to clear goblins at Desolate Mine; joins the successful mission after receiving a weapon.
027F95:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His Guild assignment, armor, and participation in clearing the mine support competent professional combat ability. The account shows no exceptional individual feat or evidence of mastery.

03E92F:Oblivion.esm.Name: Bralsa Andaren
03E92F:Oblivion.esm.Description: Bralsa Andaren is an accomplished Destruction mage and master trainer, described by another trainer as the best mage they had ever seen.
03E92F:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her actor-specific reputation and established mastery in Destruction support the Master tier. Her quest connection makes this encounter quest-related.

0A713B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Branwen
0A713B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Branwen is a Redguard monk training with Saliith to become an Arena combatant, with sustained practice in hand-to-hand fighting.
0A713B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her disciplined, near-daily sparring supports competent developing expertise as a monk, particularly in hand-to-hand combat. She is still training, with no evidence of mastery or exceptional accomplishments.

000F67:Knights.esp.Name: Brellin
000F67:Knights.esp.Description: Brellin is a crusader whose demonstrated disciplines include swordsmanship, combat magic, and ongoing melee and archery practice.
000F67:Knights.esp.Reason: He describes his blade skill as considerable, serves as a Knight of the Nine, and joins the assault on Garlas Malatar. This supports seasoned professional capability, but not mastery.
000F67:Knights.esp.Uncertainty: No exceptional individual victory or explicit master-level attainment is established.

031BC7:Oblivion.esm.Name: Bremman Senyan
031BC7:Oblivion.esm.Description: A wounded Imperial knight who remains useful in combat against Daedra during the Cheydinhal Oblivion Gate expedition.
031BC7:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His membership in the Knights of the Thorn and demonstrated usefulness in fights support competent warrior training. The expedition shows experience, but no exceptional personal feats establish higher expertise.

013623:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brevi
013623:Oblivion.esm.Description: An unused Dark Seducer intended for The Lady of Paranoia; her planned role may have involved guarding suspects.
013623:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her Dark Seducer identity and quest connection are confirmed, but the article provides no individual lore feats or established proficiency to support a combat tier.
013623:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article describes planned quest scripting, not a final-game encounter or demonstrated combat ability.

06845A:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brielus Gawey
06845A:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial commoner who works as a stablehand, tending horses and keeping watch over the corral; no exceptional professional expertise is established.
06845A:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His routine stable duties show ordinary occupational capability, but the evidence does not establish specialized training or unusual skill warranting a higher tier.

0155A4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brithaur
0155A4:Oblivion.esm.Description: Actor-specific UESP evidence could not be located to establish Brithaur’s identity or combat role.
0155A4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The available UESP search results did not identify this actor or provide evidence for a lore-based tier.
0155A4:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Without an actor-specific UESP source, Brithaur’s encounter variant and combat capabilities remain unverified.

01C166:Oblivion.esm.Name: Britta Invel
01C166:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial dinner-party guest whose recorded Acrobat class is not supported by demonstrated acrobatic expertise.
01C166:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The UESP account identifies Britta as an Imperial and notes her Acrobat class, but records no training or professional accomplishment; running after the quest spell is not evidence of expertise.
01C166:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article says Acrobat may be a default-class oversight; her actual acrobatic training is unknown.

034E72:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brodras
034E72:Oblivion.esm.Description: Brodras is a Wood Elf Fighters Guild associate, Heavy Armor trainer, and crusader who regularly spars with a fellow guildmember.
034E72:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His Fighters Guild role, regular sparring, and combat training support a competent-fighter baseline. His training is described as basic, with no evidence of mastery or exceptional feats.

00A085:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brokil gro-Shatur
00A085:Oblivion.esm.Description: An Orc commoner living a relaxed life as a regular patron of Silverhome on the Water; no specialized professional expertise is established.
00A085:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His biography and dialogue describe an ordinary inn patron, with no demonstrated specialized training or accomplishments. Tier 2 reflects the default for an adult without established specialized capability.

0477DB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Bronsila Kvinchal
0477DB:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial dockworker and commoner employed by the Imperial Trading Company in the Waterfront District.
0477DB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her long experience working on the docks supports competent professional ability in her occupation. The evidence establishes no exceptional mastery or other specialized expertise.

0231A0:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brooke
0231A0:Oblivion.esm.Description: The actor’s combat identity and capabilities could not be verified from actor-specific UESP evidence.

02991E:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brotch Calus
02991E:Oblivion.esm.Description: Retired Imperial alchemist in Bruma who provides advanced Alchemy training and directs advanced students to Sinderion.
02991E:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His advanced-trainer role, reputation as an accomplished alchemist, and referral of less advanced students establish highly accomplished professional expertise in Alchemy. Sinderion is explicitly described as more knowledgeable.

0982FC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brother Hjar
0982FC:Oblivion.esm.Description: A quiet Ancestor Moth monk and caretaker who performs routine temple duties and shares limited information about the settlement.
0982FC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His established work is temple caretaking and religious observance, supporting ordinary professional competence. The evidence does not establish exceptional skill in combat or another discipline.

0982FE:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brother Holger
0982FE:Oblivion.esm.Description: Nord Ancestor Moth caretaker who tends the temple’s silks and cemetery, knows the catacombs, and can escort visitors and unlock access.
0982FE:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His duties and practical knowledge support a competent professional monk-caretaker. The article establishes no exceptional martial or other specialized feats, so a higher tier is unsupported.

0982FD:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brother Hridi
0982FD:Oblivion.esm.Description: A competent Ancestor Moth caretaker who tends the settlement’s crops and is responsible for harvesting silk; no exceptional specialist feats are established.
0982FD:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His demonstrated professional expertise is caretaking and silk production, with a homily noted as inspiring. This supports competent capability, not mastery; there is no evidence of combat or other exceptional expertise.

033907:Oblivion.esm.Name: Brother Martin
033907:Oblivion.esm.Description: Brother Martin is a former practitioner of Daedric magic and a capable ritual scholar who later serves as a priest.
033907:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His dangerous youthful studies and successful deciphering and performance of the Mysterium Xarxes ritual establish highly accomplished Daedric scholarship and ritual expertise. His Akatosh avatar is a separate divine transformation, not evidence that his ordinary Conjurer form has comparable power.
033907:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: His past practice is described as youthful and abandoned; the article does not establish that he remains a master of combat magic.

0223AD:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His former Blade training supports basic martial preparation, but the article establishes no completed Blade career, notable combat accomplishments, or demonstrated mastery. His personal expertise is therefore best placed at the basic level.
0223AD:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The extent of his Blade training and combat ability is not established.

02DC04:Oblivion.esm.Name: Christophe Marane
02DC04:Oblivion.esm.Description: Breton innkeeper and publican who sells food, rents beds, and serves as an advanced Blunt trainer and training reference.

018DBE:Oblivion.esm.Name: Chuna
018DBE:Oblivion.esm.Description: Chuna is a Golden Saint Aurig who guards Cylarne and joins the Aureal attack or defense during the battle there.
018DBE:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her Golden Saint form and participation in organized combat establish a capable supernatural fighter. The article provides no personal feats or demonstrated mastery to support an exceptional tier.

015EA7:Oblivion.esm.Name: Cicero Verus
015EA7:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial commoner who earns a living distributing copies of the Black Horse Courier.
015EA7:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His work shows routine reliability, but the evidence establishes no specialized professional expertise or exceptional accomplishments. As an ordinary adult without established specialized training, tier 2 is appropriate.

01ECD8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ciindil
01ECD8:Oblivion.esm.Description: Wood Elf assassin and Mephala worshipper at Mephala’s Shrine; carries an iron dagger. No exceptional personal accomplishments are established.
01ECD8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her identity and class establish the assassin profession, supporting competent professional capability. The evidence does not establish exceptional mastery or accomplishments.

0135B7:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ciirta
0135B7:Oblivion.esm.Description: Ciirta is a powerful magician and capable fighter who survived the Greymarch and can defend herself with a broad range of magic.
0135B7:Oblivion.esm.Reason: UESP describes her as a powerful magician and strong fighter, with substantial magical and defensive resources. This supports an elite combatant rating without relying on quest importance or gameplay scaling.

015588:Oblivion.esm.Name: Cindanwe
015588:Oblivion.esm.Description: Cindanwe is a quest-related Altmer farm foreperson whose demonstrated expertise lies in managing and coercing workers, not supernatural mind-reading or combat.
015588:Oblivion.esm.Reason: She runs Fellmoor’s water-root operation and manipulates workers through paranoia and control, supporting competent professional capability. Her claimed mind-reading is a deception; exceptional magical, combat, or other specialist mastery is not established.

002E95:Oblivion.esm.Name: Cingaer
002E95:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Bosmer thief and member of the Hrota Cave gang who attacks intruders and uses a bow in combat.
002E95:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His established role as a thief supports competent professional capability, with a bow as a demonstrated combat discipline. The evidence does not establish exceptional mastery.
002E95:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: No specific theft or stealth accomplishments are described.

034E86:Oblivion.esm.Name: Cingor
034E86:Oblivion.esm.Description: Wood Elf crusader and Fighters Guild member who patrols Leyawiin and becomes hostile after the Dagon Shrine quest.
034E86:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His Fighters Guild membership, warhammer, and combat magic support a competent-fighter baseline, but the article records no exceptional combat feats or demonstrated mastery.

035EB8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Cirroc
035EB8:Oblivion.esm.Description: Cirroc is Bruma’s resident chapel healer, a Restoration trainer, and the chapel’s contact in the quest to recover the Stone of St. Alessia.

000F84:Knights.esp.Name: Lathon
000F84:Knights.esp.Description: Lathon is Sir Roderic’s squire who later joins the Knights of the Nine and fights alongside them.
000F84:Knights.esp.Reason: Nearly two years as a squire, ongoing sword practice, and participation in battles against a wraith and Aurorans support competent, developing knightly ability. His own dialogue says he is not yet ready when first offered knighthood.
000F84:Knights.esp.Uncertainty: His capability develops across the quest: the initial squire and later knighted states are both represented.

0038CA:Oblivion.esm.Name: Laythe Wavrick
0038CA:Oblivion.esm.Description: Laythe Wavrick is Chorrol’s Chief Herald and Countess Valga’s attendant, responsible for guiding visitors and maintaining court etiquette.
0038CA:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His dialogue and duties show competent professional knowledge of court procedure, heraldry, and Chorrol’s history. The evidence supports competence, not exceptional mastery.

028E72:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lazare Milvan
028E72:Oblivion.esm.Description: A wealthy, secluded Breton noble who carries a silver longsword and challenges others to duels, but has no established professional specialty or demonstrated accomplishment.
028E72:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His identity and noble standing are clear, but wealth and rank do not establish expertise. The sword challenge suggests some willingness to fight, yet no combat skill or other specialized capability is demonstrated.
028E72:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article does not establish his actual training or ability with a sword.

015D87:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lazy Kaslowyn
015D87:Oblivion.esm.Description: Chorrol beggar who provides Thieves Guild clues and serves as a quest-related contact for speechcraft training.
015D87:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His established role is that of an ordinary commoner beggar. No specialized professional expertise or exceptional personal capability is documented; providing clues and being a training prerequisite do not establish mastery.

18AD70:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lenka Valus
18AD70:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial commoner and Kvatch refugee; no specialized professional discipline or notable expertise is established.
18AD70:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies Lenka as a commoner who seeks refuge and follows other survivors to safety. It provides no evidence of specialized training or accomplishments, so the ordinary-adult baseline applies.
18AD70:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Evidence about her capabilities is limited to her civilian role and behavior during the crisis.

181C68:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lerexus Callidus
181C68:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Leyawiin City Guard and Imperial Legion member investigating Skooma dealers; equipped with Legion armor, a silver longsword, and a shield.
181C68:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His guard and Legion service support competent professional capability. His investigation shows persistence, but he is repeatedly spotted by a lookout and delegates the raid; no exceptional personal expertise is established.

018C68:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lewin Tilwald
018C68:Oblivion.esm.Description: Breton rogue and adventurer who has stolen from Norbert Lelles and fights with a shortsword and bow during the Xedilian quest.
018C68:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His rogue identity, reported theft, and participation in an expedition support basic professional capability. He shows no evidence of exceptional stealth, combat, or other advanced expertise.

016053:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ley Marillin
016053:Oblivion.esm.Description: A competent Imperial City innkeeper who operates the well-regarded King and Queen Tavern and handles lodging and sales.
016053:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His established publican work and the tavern’s positive reputation support professional competence in hospitality and trade, but not exceptional mastery.

00A0B8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Leyawiin City Watch
00A0B8:Oblivion.esm.Description: A generic Leyawiin City Watch guard serving as a soldier under the local Count.
00A0B8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The UESP article identifies county city guards as soldiers of their local Count. This supports the professional-soldier baseline, with no evidence of exceptional individual ability.

035F8E:Oblivion.esm.Description: Leyawiin Castle jail guard equipped with a silver mace and guard armor; part of the ordinary Imperial jailor role.
035F8E:Oblivion.esm.Reason: A jailor is a guard, so the professional-soldier baseline supports competent combat ability. No individual feats or exceptional training are established.

026F20:Oblivion.esm.Name: Leyawiin Soldier
026F20:Oblivion.esm.Description: A unique Leyawiin Imperial guard sent to defend Bruma, equipped with a steel longsword and guard armor.
026F20:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies this actor as an Imperial guard serving in the defense of Bruma. A professional soldier fits the project’s competent-fighter baseline.

01E5EC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lich
01E5EC:Oblivion.esm.Description: A full lich, a formidable undead spellcaster whose necromantic mastery makes it exceptionally dangerous.
01E5EC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor is the ordinary Lich creature form, not a lesser Nether Lich. The project’s verified-lich baseline assigns tier 6 for its inherent necromantic mastery.

0823B5:Oblivion.esm.Name: Limark
0823B5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Limark is a Redguard knight whose ghost is encountered on the Hill of Suicides and can be freed by returning his skull.
0823B5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His knight identity supports competent professional capability, but the article establishes no exceptional martial feats. His ghostly fatigue-fortifying reward is a supernatural effect, not evidence of greater knightly expertise.

185374:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lithnilian
185374:Oblivion.esm.Description: Altmer sorcerer and Welkynd Stone scholar whose decade of research culminated in a novel discovery in a natural cave.
185374:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His sustained, original research demonstrates seasoned scholarly expertise, and he is identified as a sorcerer. The evidence supports a capable professional, but establishes no rare magical mastery or extraordinary combat accomplishment.

00A293:Oblivion.esm.Name: Llensi Llaram
00A293:Oblivion.esm.Description: Dark Elf scout and Fighters Guild newcomer in Anvil; no distinctive combat accomplishments are documented.
00A293:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article describes her as a newcomer who prefers watching other members train over improving her own combat skills. A basic ordinary-mortal rating is appropriate.

0034DF:Oblivion.esm.Name: Llevana Nedaren
0034DF:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Cheydinhal farmer whose quest-specific plan uses paralysis and pet rats to kill Ulrich Leland.
0034DF:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her demonstrated ability to paralyze a guard captain and direct a lethal attack shows seasoned practical capability beyond ordinary farming, but does not establish broad or master-level expertise.
0034DF:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article describes a quest-specific feat, not the breadth or repeatability of her magical skill.

03C9C3:Oblivion.esm.Name: Llevana's Tunnel Rat
03C9C3:Oblivion.esm.Description: One of Llevana Nedaren’s rats, summoned during a quest to attack a paralyzed guard captain.
03C9C3:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor is confirmed as a rat, with no evidence of unusual abilities or combat prowess. Its quest role does not establish exceptional strength.

035EB1:Oblivion.esm.Name: Logvaar
035EB1:Oblivion.esm.Description: Logvaar is a Nord warrior employed as a bouncer at the Jerall View Inn in Bruma.
035EB1:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His bouncer role and responsibility for handling troublemakers support competent professional-level security and combat capability. The article establishes no exceptional martial feats or mastery.

000F96:Knights.esp.Description: Lord Berich Vlindrel appears as a hostile gloom wraith in Underpall Cave during the Crusader’s relic quests.
000F96:Knights.esp.Reason: The actor-specific UESP article confirms this encounter form is a gloom wraith, matching the project’s PowerTier 6 baseline. This rates the hostile wraith, not Berich’s later non-hostile ghost form.

01EC31:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lord Drad
01EC31:Oblivion.esm.Description: A noble and mine owner whose demonstrated expertise is managing his estate and profitable mining operation, not combat.
01EC31:Oblivion.esm.Reason: He operates a productive farm and mine, acquired the mine and land, and oversees the ogre labor that extracts its gold. This supports competent business and estate-management capability, but not exceptional mastery.

00E824:DLCBattlehornCastle.esp.Name: Lord Kain
00E824:DLCBattlehornCastle.esp.Description: Lord Kain is a unique skeletal warrior whose failed restoration left him, in the article’s words, a Skeleton Hero; he retains his distinctive sword and shield.
00E824:DLCBattlehornCastle.esp.Reason: The UESP article confirms his Skeleton Hero form, matching the project’s tier-4 baseline for an experienced skeletal warrior. His former leadership alone does not justify a higher tier.

013417:DLCBattlehornCastle.esp.Name: Lord Kelvyn
013417:DLCBattlehornCastle.esp.Description: Lord Kelvyn was a Redguard knight and lord of Battlehorn Castle, later killed by marauders.
013417:DLCBattlehornCastle.esp.Reason: His identity as a knight supports competent professional capability in that discipline. His title, equipment, and death establish no exceptional martial accomplishment or mastery.
013417:DLCBattlehornCastle.esp.Uncertainty: The article provides no specific evidence of his combat training or deeds.

038EDD:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lord Lovidicus
038EDD:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial noble and centuries-old vampire encountered as a starving, hostile prisoner during the Gray Prince’s quest.
038EDD:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His vampirism establishes supernatural abilities, but the article documents no specialized professional mastery or exceptional accomplishments. His noble identity and long isolation do not establish greater expertise.

00BE7F:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lord Rugdumph gro-Shurgak
00BE7F:Oblivion.esm.Description: An Orcish noble and Fighters Guild client; no specialized combat, magical, stealth, or other professional expertise is established.
00BE7F:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The evidence identifies him as a wealthy noble whose role is requesting his daughter’s rescue. His title and quest importance do not establish personal mastery; ordinary capability is the best-supported tier.

0823BA:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lorenz Bog-Trotter
0823BA:Oblivion.esm.Description: Lorenz Bog-Trotter is a restless ghost, formerly a Nord knight, encountered on the Hill of Suicides and releasable by returning his skull.
0823BA:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article confirms his ghost form, matching the project’s tier-3 ghost baseline. His former knight identity is not accompanied by specific feats or mastery supporting a higher tier.

06E7EF:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lorgren Benirus
06E7EF:Oblivion.esm.Description: Lorgren is a necromancer who became a lich, prolonged his life with stolen souls, created manor ghosts, and planned to destroy Anvil.
06E7EF:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His lich transformation, soul-based life extension, and creation of supernatural guardians establish rare mastery in necromancy. This assesses his necromantic expertise, not equal strength across all disciplines.
06E7EF:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: This record is Lorgren’s disembodied voice; the article establishes his necromantic history but describes the attacking lich as a later manifestation.
06E7EF:Oblivion.esm.DelevelingReview: Disembodied monologue NPC; the separate lich combat form is already handled.

0855A4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lorgren Benirus
0855A4:Oblivion.esm.Description: Lorgren Benirus appears as a lich, a former mage who practiced necromancy, created guardian ghosts, and sought immortality.
0855A4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His transformation into a lich and demonstrated necromantic work support master-level power. His plan to destroy Anvil was stopped by the Mages Guild, but the article gives limited evidence of his direct combat feats.

04DE82:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lorkmir
04DE82:Oblivion.esm.Description: Lorkmir is a slain Nord warrior whose corpse is found in his Imperial City home; the article establishes no active or supernatural combat form.
04DE82:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The verified encounter is his corpse, not a living warrior. The article says he has been slain and provides no evidence that his body can fight or has been animated.

00A10A:Oblivion.esm.Name: Luciana Galena
00A10A:Oblivion.esm.Description: Bravil Thieves Guild fence and advanced Light Armor trainer, recognized for practical armor knowledge and above-average fencing.
00A10A:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her advanced-trainer status and townspeople’s reports of substantial Light Armor experience support seasoned expertise. Guild leaders call her a decent fence, better than Ongar and Dar Jee; this supports competence in fencing, not legendary mastery.

0034AF:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lucien Lachance
0034AF:Oblivion.esm.Description: Lucien Lachance is an Imperial assassin and Speaker of the Black Hand. This Hunted variant is the fugitive encountered during Following a Lead.
0034AF:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His established career as a professional assassin and his training of Shadowscales support an elite specialist rating. The article does not establish power on a legendary or supernatural scale.
0034AF:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: No direct duel or demonstrated feat establishes his combat ability beyond the elite-assassin level.

0224ED:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lucien Lachance
0224ED:Oblivion.esm.Description: An accomplished Imperial assassin and Black Hand Speaker who trained Shadowscales; this is the original Lucien Lachance, not his later hunted variant.
0224ED:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His assassin training and experience support an elite specialist rating. His leadership title alone does not establish greater combat power, and the article gives no evidence that he approaches legendary combatants.

015D86:Oblivion.esm.Name: Luckless Lucina
015D86:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial beggar in Cheydinhal who provides information about the Thieves Guild and assists during The Elven Maiden quest.
015D86:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her established role is that of a commoner beggar, with limited combat resources and no demonstrated specialized mastery. Providing information and quest assistance do not establish exceptional expertise.

0234BF:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lum gro-Baroth
0234BF:Oblivion.esm.Description: An Orc warrior in Chorrol who trains daily with a warhammer and bow, spars regularly, and offers advanced Block training.
0234BF:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His regular weapons practice, sparring, and advanced instruction establish him as a seasoned combatant, but not a master-level trainer.
0234BF:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article provides no specific combat feats establishing a higher tier.

01DFB3:Oblivion.esm.Name: Lumdum gro-Golpok

02D01A:Oblivion.esm.Name: Marc Gulitte
02D01A:Oblivion.esm.Description: Marc Gulitte is an experienced Mages Guild mage and advanced Destruction instructor, though the article establishes no exceptional combat feats or mastery.
02D01A:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His advanced Destruction instruction and reputation as Anvil’s foremost fireball caster support a seasoned specialist rating. His relaxed civilian life and lack of demonstrated combat feats do not support a higher tier.

0A345B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Marcel Amelion
0A345B:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Breton farmer in Water’s Edge who survives the village’s destruction and mourns his daughter.
0A345B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His established occupation is farming, with no evidence of specialized combat or other exceptional professional expertise. Tier 2 reflects an ordinary adult with no established specialized training.

01ECAB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Maren the Seal
01ECAB:Oblivion.esm.Description: Maren the Seal is a hunter and Peryite worshipper encountered among the trapped souls in Peryite’s Realm.
01ECAB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her identity establishes hunting as her profession, supporting competent professional capability. The record gives no evidence of exceptional hunting feats or mastery.

034E81:Oblivion.esm.Name: Margarte
034E81:Oblivion.esm.Description: Leyawiin merchant and advanced Mercantile trainer, known for business expertise and alchemical ingredient-gathering and experimentation.
034E81:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her advanced Mercantile training and reputation as knowledgeable about business support seasoned professional expertise. Her alchemical interest is evident, but no exceptional alchemy accomplishment is established.

033904:Oblivion.esm.Name: Marguerite Diel
033904:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Breton Mythic Dawn adept who appears in the Imperial City with orders to kill the player, using bound equipment, a Daedra summon, shielding, and shock magic.
033904:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her adept identity and combat-magic repertoire establish trained, competent professional capability. The evidence supports practical magical combat expertise, but not exceptional mastery or extraordinary accomplishments.

0034C2:Oblivion.esm.Name: Mariana Ancharia
0034C2:Oblivion.esm.Description: Mariana is a professional innkeeper and publican, experienced in hospitality, room rentals, and local upper-class society.
0034C2:Oblivion.esm.Reason: She operates a fashionable inn, serves its clientele, and demonstrates familiarity with Cheydinhal’s notable residents. This supports competent professional ability in hospitality and local knowledge, not exceptional mastery.

0327BB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Marie Alouette
0327BB:Oblivion.esm.Description: Breton herder in Water’s Edge; the quest scripts her death, while a goblin replacement is involved in the encounter.
0327BB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her established profession is herding, but the article gives no evidence of exceptional professional expertise or specialized combat capability. Her bow and arrows alone do not establish advanced skill.

028F9F:Oblivion.esm.Name: Marie Palielle
028F9F:Oblivion.esm.Description: Sister Marie Palielle is Skingrad’s chapel healer, tending to the sick and injured and providing basic Restoration training.
028F9F:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her ongoing professional healing duties support competent practical Restoration expertise. She is explicitly only a basic trainer, with no evidence of exceptional mastery or broader combat capability.

0038B3:Oblivion.esm.Name: Mariette Rielle
0038B3:Oblivion.esm.Description: Mariette Rielle is a Breton necromancer of the Order of the Black Worm encountered at Nenyond Twyll during a related quest.
0038B3:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her established necromancer role and reliance on necromantic spells support competent professional capability. The evidence does not establish exceptional personal feats or mastery.

01605E:Oblivion.esm.Name: Marinus Catiotus
01605E:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial commoner with no established specialized training or demonstrated professional expertise.
01605E:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His biography presents him as a comfortable civilian. He claims to earn money at the Arena, but the article notes he is never found there; no related expertise is established.

0280CB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Marlena Brussiner
0280CB:Oblivion.esm.Description: An Imperial hunter and Hackdirt cultist involved in the events surrounding Dar-Ma’s disappearance.
0280CB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her identified profession supports competent hunter-level capability. The article documents cult involvement and an iron mace, but no exceptional hunting or combat accomplishments.
0280CB:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: No specific hunting feats or demonstrated specialist skills are documented.

015EAC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Maro Rufus
015EAC:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial City light-armor specialist and shopkeeper with a strong reputation; personal smithing mastery is not established.
015EAC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His specialization and the shop’s reputation support seasoned professional expertise in light-armor trade. The article does not attribute exceptional crafting feats to him; it identifies Gin-Wulm as the smith who makes and maintains the armor.
015EAC:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: His reputation is well supported, but the extent of his personal smithing skill is unclear.

034EB5:Oblivion.esm.Name: Martina Floria
034EB5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial sorceress and Mages Guild master trainer whose Illusion mastery is praised by other skilled illusionists.
034EB5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Actor-specific dialogue identifies Martina as having truly mastered Illusion, and another guild head says her mastery surpasses her own. This supports rare magical mastery.

00A08B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Marz
00A08B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Argonian chapel healer and advanced Restoration trainer in Bravil, known for effective healing and teaching.
00A08B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Marz is an established professional healer: she provides advanced Restoration training, and Bravil residents describe her as excellent and gifted. This supports seasoned expertise, but not rare mastery.

00398A:Oblivion.esm.Name: Mathieu Bellamont
00398A:Oblivion.esm.Description: A highly accomplished Breton assassin and Black Hand member whose long-planned vendetta culminates in killing two Black Hand members before confronting the player.
00398A:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His assassin skills earned him promotion to the Black Hand; he secretly killed Brotherhood members and Lucien Lachance, then personally slew Belisarius Arius and Banus Alor during his final attack.

0277D5:Oblivion.esm.Name: Matilde Petit
0277D5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Matilde Petit is a Breton noble and guest involved in the Whodunit? quest at Summitmist Manor.
0277D5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her noble identity and social conduct are established, but the article provides no evidence of specialized professional expertise or notable accomplishments. Her occasional attack is not a demonstrated feat.

030FDA:Oblivion.esm.Name: Matthias Draconis
030FDA:Oblivion.esm.Description: Umbacano’s working guard and enforcer; a rough-and-tumble professional whose established role is patrolling and guarding the manor.
030FDA:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His regular guard duties and enforcer role support competent professional capability. The evidence establishes no exceptional combat, stealth, or other specialist mastery; the tier reflects his demonstrated guard profession, not an assumption that he excels equally in every discipline.

085969:Oblivion.esm.Name: Mazoga the Orc
085969:Oblivion.esm.Description: Mazoga is a former outlaw turned aspiring knight who pursues bandits and fights with sword and heavy armor.
085969:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her past association with Black Brugo and her pursuit of Mogens and other bandits establish practical, competent fighting experience. Her record supports a professional level, but not exceptional mastery.

0878B1:Oblivion.esm.Name: Medrike
0878B1:Oblivion.esm.Description: Medrike is a Xivilai guarding the exit to the Forbidden Grotto in Mankar Camoran’s Paradise.
0878B1:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The UESP article confirms Medrike’s Xivilai form, which matches the project’s tier-6 baseline. His quest role does not add a separate power bonus.

01E64E:Oblivion.esm.Name: Mehrunes Dagon
01E64E:Oblivion.esm.Description: Mehrunes Dagon’s direct, gigantic manifestation at the Temple of the One during the Oblivion Crisis.

015D88:Oblivion.esm.Name: Nermus the Mooch

0BB9CB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Nerussa

035740:Oblivion.esm.Name: Newheim the Portly

01ECC8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Nivan Dalvilu

07B7D5:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Pale Pass encounter in ordinary ogre form: a huge, unarmed humanoid whose species is described as having tremendous strength.
07B7D5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The supplied UESP article describes ogres as huge and tremendously strong, supporting a dangerous natural combat threat. No unique feats are established for this encounter.
07B7D5:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: No actor-specific UESP page was found; the tier relies on the supplied record’s Ogre identity and the general species description.

015EA8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Palonirya
015EA8:Oblivion.esm.Description: A renowned clothier and master merchant, noted for her clothing designs and exceptional bargaining expertise.
015EA8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her explicit master-trainer status establishes mastery in Mercantile, reinforced by her reputation as a tough negotiator and successful designer. This tier reflects professional expertise, not combat ability.

0293E4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Parwen
0293E4:Oblivion.esm.Description: Parwen is a trained Fighters Guild archer who hunts goblins and practices dagger sparring, though she describes herself as not a great archer.
0293E4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her regular weapons training and experience killing goblins establish her as a capable combatant, but the article provides no evidence of veteran or elite mastery.

0A3164:Oblivion.esm.Name: Pelagius
0A3164:Oblivion.esm.Description: An Imperial Blade at Cloud Ruler Temple who spends the day sparring with Fortis.
0A3164:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His regular sparring supports competent professional blade and defensive training, but no exceptional personal accomplishments establish greater expertise. This tier reflects his demonstrated combat discipline, not equal mastery of other skills.

000F88:Knights.esp.Name: Pelinal Whitestrake
000F88:Knights.esp.Description: A vision of Pelinal Whitestrake appears after the Pilgrimage and directs the player toward his lost shrine.
000F88:Knights.esp.Reason: The historical Pelinal slew Umaril with divine aid, but this actor is his quest vision, not the living warrior. The article provides no evidence that the vision can fight.
000F88:Knights.esp.Uncertainty: The vision’s combat capability is not established, so a combat tier cannot be recommended.

015D7F:Oblivion.esm.Name: Penniless Olvus
015D7F:Oblivion.esm.Description: An Anvil beggar who offers Thieves Guild information and relies on fists if attacked.
015D7F:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article establishes ordinary beggar duties and limited combat, but no specialized mastery or exceptional accomplishment. Quest assistance does not establish advanced thieving or speech expertise.

01D356:Oblivion.esm.Name: Pennus Mallius
01D356:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial commoner and former adventurer who earned substantial treasure during multiple travels, now retired to a comfortable life in the Imperial City.
01D356:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His successful expeditions support competent practical adventuring ability, but the evidence establishes no exceptional feats or specific mastery in combat, magic, stealth, or another discipline.
01D356:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: His expedition methods and individual skills are not described.

030FDC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Perennia Draconis
030FDC:Oblivion.esm.Description: Elderly Imperial farmer at Applewatch who regularly tends her vegetable patch with farm tools.
030FDC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her daily farm work supports competent professional farming capability. The evidence shows no exceptional agricultural mastery or notable combat, stealth, or other specialized expertise.

035EAD:Oblivion.esm.Name: Petrine
035EAD:Oblivion.esm.Description: Petrine is a Nord ostler who runs Wildeye Stables and sells Paint horses outside Bruma.
035EAD:Oblivion.esm.Reason: She demonstrates competent stablekeeping and horse sales, handling the business while her employee tends the horses. No exceptional equestrian or commercial expertise is established.
035EAD:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Her specific horse-handling skill is not demonstrated; this tier reflects competent professional work.

0B1681:Oblivion.esm.Name: Philip Franc
0B1681:Oblivion.esm.Description: A working hunter with practical bow-and-arrow equipment, but no established exceptional accomplishments.
0B1681:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His identity as a hunter and his bow-and-arrow gear support competent professional hunting ability. The article provides no evidence of mastery or extraordinary feats; this tier concerns his hunting expertise, not universal combat prowess.

015E9B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Phintias
015E9B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Redguard bookseller and rare-book specialist who owns the Imperial City’s First Edition bookstore.
015E9B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His extensive knowledge of rare books is recognized by others, and he identifies and handles an exceptionally rare volume sought during a major quest. This supports highly accomplished expertise in bookselling and rare-book knowledge, not general combat mastery.

00A29D:Oblivion.esm.Name: Pinarus Inventius
00A29D:Oblivion.esm.Description: Anvil’s reputedly most experienced huntsman, known for exceptional tracking and deadly, highly accomplished marksmanship.
00A29D:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Town rumors describe him as deadly with a bow and able to shoot a bird in flight. His hunting expertise and advanced marksman training support an elite specialist rating.

02AE7B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies the crew as cutlass-armed but provides no specific combat training or exceptional feats for this pirate. The ordinary adult mortal baseline is appropriate.

016054:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial commoner and nominal tavern server with no established specialized expertise or accomplishments.
016054:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The UESP account identifies her as a commoner and describes tavern work and frequent Arena gambling, but establishes no notable professional training or capability.

00D44B:DLCBattlehornCastle.esp.Name: Plautis Rusonius
00D44B:DLCBattlehornCastle.esp.Description: Imperial priest serving as Battlehorn Castle’s cook; his evidenced professional expertise is culinary.
00D44B:DLCBattlehornCastle.esp.Reason: He managed the Tiber Septim Hotel kitchens for many years and is personally recommended as an excellent cook, supporting highly accomplished culinary skill.

14683E:Oblivion.esm.Name: Porkchop
14683E:Oblivion.esm.Description: Porkchop is an Arena boar who fights alongside the player in the final Yellow Team match and can defeat an opponent.

0389BD:Oblivion.esm.Description: Retired Redguard gladiator and master Heavy Armor trainer, now living at the Roxey Inn.

01D355:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial commoner with no established specialized profession or exceptional personal accomplishments.
01D355:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her biography and dialogue establish an ordinary, quiet civilian life, with no demonstrated specialized training or professional expertise. Tier 2 reflects an ordinary adult, not a finding of negligible capability.

000F9A:Knights.esp.Name: Umaril
000F9A:Knights.esp.Description: Umaril is an ancient Ayleid sorcerer-king, empowered by Meridia with an immortal spirit that survives the destruction of his physical form.

000F9B:Knights.esp.Name: Umaril

000F9C:Knights.esp.Name: Umaril
000F9C:Knights.esp.Description: Umaril is the returned physical form of an Ayleid sorcerer-king, born of an Ayleid mother and divine father, whose alliance with Meridia lets his spirit survive bodily defeat.
000F9C:Knights.esp.Reason: His extraordinary lineage, ancient rule, and demonstrated ability to survive Pelinal’s defeat and return support mythic power. He remains below the greatest divine powers: his physical form can be defeated, and his spirit requires separate destruction.

000F9D:Knights.esp.Name: Umaril
000F9D:Knights.esp.Description: Ayleid sorcerer-king bound to Meridia, Umaril is an immortal-returning supernatural foe who commands Aurorans and must be defeated in both physical and spiritual forms.
000F9D:Knights.esp.Reason: His supernatural survival and the need for a divinely empowered Crusader to destroy both body and spirit support Mythic power. His defeat by Pelinal and the Crusader keeps him below Apex.

000F9E:Knights.esp.Name: Umaril

000F9E:Knights.esp.Reason: His immortality and return across realms, combined with the need to defeat both his body and spirit, support Mythic power. His defeat by Pelinal keeps him below the Overwhelming tier.

000F9F:Knights.esp.Name: Umaril

000F9F:Knights.esp.Reason: His ancient rule, sorcerous power, divine parentage, Meridia-backed return from death, and the extraordinary efforts required to defeat him support mythic power, below deity-level anchors.
